gaps.explanation: 'What I meant' means 'the thing that I meant'; 'that I meant' would be an incomplete relative clause.

gaps.sentence: There is nothing ___ I would change about the design.
gaps.explanation: After 'nothing', use 'that' (or omit the pronoun); 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: ___ surprised me most was his calm.
gaps.hint: 'what' = the thing that; the sentence has no other subject
gaps.explanation: 'What' means 'the thing that' and acts as subject: 'What surprised me most ...' — 'that' cannot introduce this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: He repaired the car ___ engine had failed.
gaps.hint: the engine belongs to the car
gaps.explanation: 'Whose engine' means 'the car's engine', showing possession even with objects.

gaps.sentence: His latest film, ___ was shot entirely in Iceland, won three awards.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is the subject pronoun for the film; 'that' never appears in non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.

gaps.sentence: Have you met the couple ___ son is in your class?
gaps.hint: the son belongs to the couple
gaps.explanation: 'Whose son' means 'their son'; the possessive relative 'whose' is required.

gaps.sentence: It is one of the most impressive buildings ___ I have ever seen.
gaps.explanation: After superlative expressions, 'that' is the standard relative pronoun in defining clauses.
